newsitem.title: USA: Harvard unit seeks damages from Calgene CGNE,O.
newsitem.headline: Harvard unit seeks damages from Calgene CGNE,O.

text.p: A wholly owned subsidiary of Harvard University has sued Calgene Inc for damages of $8.8 million alleging Calgene failed to honor a 1994 stock purchase agreement.

In papers filed Wednesday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Harvard's Fletcher Capital Markets Inc of Cambridge, Mass., said the agreement gave it the right to buy 2.3 million shares of Calgene for $10 million or $4.25 a share.

On March 31, Monsanto Co agreed to acquire the 45.4 percent of Calgene it does not already own for $240 million or $8 a share. The tender offer closes Friday, but a Calgene spokeswoman said the lawsuit "won't have any effect on the merger."

In court papers, Fletcher said it "has wrongfully been prevented from tendering 2.3 million shares of Calgene common stock to Monsanto in the tender offer" and may be precluded from having the stock included in the count of shares outstanding. Fletcher's stock would represent 3.4 percent of Calgene's fully diluted outstanding shares.

Fletcher, which Harvard received as a charitable gift in December, 1994, wants the court to award legal expenses and damages at least equal to the difference between the agreement price of $4.25 a share and Monsanto's offer of $8 a share.
The Calgene spokeswoman told Reuters that President Lloyd Kunimoto said "Our understanding is that the (Harvard) claim has no merit."
